description: The magnetic-field direction crosses horizontal BC at the normal origin; alpha and 90 degrees minus alpha are complementary sectors at the same vertex.

authoritativeText.text:
如果导体在不随时间改变的磁场中运动，导体中的感生电动势就不是由涡旋电场产生的，而是由另一种原因产生的。

当导体运动时，自由电子也随导体一起运动。
因此，磁场对电荷施加洛仑兹力。

这个力使导体内部的电荷移动。
因此，这种感生电动势具有“磁性起源”。

在地球上的许多发电站中，正是洛仑兹力使运动导体中的电子移动。

现在计算匀强磁场中矩形回路的感生电动势（图290）。
设回路的一边$AB=l$，以恒定速度$\vec{v}$沿着$BC$和$AD$两边滑动。

导体AB始终与$CD$边平行。
磁感应强度$\vec{B}$与导体$AB$垂直，并与导体的速度成$\alpha$角。

图290

磁场对运动带电粒子的作用力（参阅§121），其大小为

$f=|q|vB\sin\alpha$。
(12-5)

这个由导体运动引起的有效力沿导体$AB$的方向作用。
为计算电动势，将式(12-5)中的有效力沿电荷相对于导体的路程$l$积分，得到：

$A=f\cdot l=|q|vBl\sin\alpha$。
这里的A是电荷相对于导体运动时的有效力积分，不是磁场对载流子沿总位移所做的功。
磁力垂直于载流子的总速度，包括随导体运动和在导体内运动这两部分，所以不对载流子做总功。

维持导体$AB$运动的外部机械推动者做功，向电路提供电能。
感生电动势等于上述导体相对的有效力积分除以电荷量的大小：

$\mathcal{E}_i=\frac{A}{|q|}=vBl\sin\alpha$。
(12-6)

这个公式适用于上述几何条件下，在匀强磁场中以速度$v$运动、长度为$l$的直导体。
直杆沿v与B的叉乘方向放置，即同时垂直于v和B；
alpha是v与B之间的夹角。

回路中其余导体的电动势为零，因为它们没有运动。
因此，整个回路$ABCD$的电动势等于$\mathcal{E}_i$(12-6)。

如果速度$v$恒定，电动势就保持不变。
此时电流增大，因为导体$AB$向右移动时，回路的总电阻减小。

另一方面，也可以利用电磁感应定律(12-4)计算感生电动势。
实际上，通过回路$ABCD$的磁通量为
$\Phi=BS\cos(90^\circ-\alpha)=BS\sin\alpha$。

其中，$90^\circ-\alpha$是矢量$\vec{B}$与回路表面法线$\vec{n}$之间的夹角（图291），$S$是回路$ABCD$的面积。
如果在初始时刻$(t=0)$，导体$AB$与导体$CD$之间的距离为$BC$（图290），那么导体移动时，回路面积按下式改变：

图291

$S=AB(BC-vt)$。

在$\Delta t$时间内，回路面积的改变量为
$\Delta S=-lv\Delta t$。
负号表示面积减小。

在这段时间内，磁通量的变化量为
$\Delta\Phi=-Blv\Delta t$ $\sin\alpha$。
因此，

$\mathcal{E}_i=-\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}=Blv\sin\alpha$，

这与前面得到的结果相同（公式12-6）。

如果整个回路$ABCD$在匀强磁场中运动，并保持相对于矢量$\vec{B}$的方向不变，回路中的感生电动势就为零，因为穿过回路的磁通量不变。
也可以这样解释：回路运动时，力作用在导体$AB$和$CD$中的电子上，方向分别为从$B$到$A$和从$C$到$D$。
沿回路顺时针或逆时针走一周时，这些力所做的总功为零。

When a conductor moves in a magnetic field that does not change with time, the induced EMF in the conductor is caused not by a vortex electric field, but by another mechanism.

As the conductor moves, its free electrons move with it. The magnetic field therefore exerts the Lorentz force on the charges.
This force moves charges inside the conductor. The induced EMF thus has a "magnetic origin."

At many power stations on Earth, it is the Lorentz force that moves electrons in moving conductors.

We now calculate the induced EMF in a rectangular circuit in a uniform magnetic field (Figure 290). Let one side of the circuit, $AB=l$, slide at a constant velocity $\vec{v}$ along sides $BC$ and $AD$.
The conductor AB remains parallel to side $CD$ at all times. The magnetic induction $\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to conductor $AB$ and makes an angle $\alpha$ with its velocity.

Figure 290

The magnitude of the force exerted by the magnetic field on a moving charged particle (see §121) is

$f=|q|vB\sin\alpha$. (12-5)

The motion-induced effective force acts along conductor $AB$. For the EMF calculation, integrate the effective force in (12-5) over the charge's displacement $l$ relative to the conductor:

$A=f\cdot l=|q|vBl\sin\alpha$.
Here A is the effective-force integral for motion relative to the conductor, not the total magnetic work on a carrier. The magnetic force is perpendicular to the carrier's total velocity, including motion with and within the conductor, so it does no total work on the carrier.

The external mechanical agent maintaining the motion of conductor $AB$ supplies the electrical energy. The induced EMF is the conductor-relative effective-force integral per unit charge magnitude:

$\mathcal{E}_i=\frac{A}{|q|}=vBl\sin\alpha$. (12-6)

This formula applies to a straight conductor moving at speed $v$ in a uniform magnetic field and having length $l$, under the geometric conditions above. The rod lies along v cross B, perpendicular to both v and B;
alpha is the angle between v and B.

The EMF in the other conductors of the circuit is zero because they are not moving. The EMF in the entire circuit $ABCD$ therefore equals $\mathcal{E}_i$ in (12-6).
If the speed $v$ is constant, the EMF remains constant. The current then increases because the total resistance of the circuit decreases as conductor $AB$ moves to the right.

The induced EMF can also be calculated using the law of electromagnetic induction (12-4). The magnetic flux through circuit $ABCD$ is
$\Phi=BS\cos(90^\circ-\alpha)=BS\sin\alpha$.
Here, $90^\circ-\alpha$ is the angle between vector $\vec{B}$ and the normal $\vec{n}$ to the surface of the circuit (Figure 291), and $S$ is the area of circuit $ABCD$. If, at the initial instant $(t=0)$, the distance between conductors $AB$ and $CD$ is $BC$ (Figure 290), then the area changes as the conductor moves according to

Figure 291

$S=AB(BC-vt)$.

During a time interval $\Delta t$, the change in the area of the circuit is
$\Delta S=-lv\Delta t$.

The minus sign indicates that the area decreases. The change in magnetic flux during this interval is
$\Delta\Phi=-Blv\Delta t$ $\sin\alpha$.
Therefore,

$\mathcal{E}_i=-\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}=Blv\sin\alpha$,

This is the same result obtained earlier in formula (12-6).

If the entire circuit $ABCD$ moves in a uniform magnetic field while maintaining its orientation relative to vector $\vec{B}$, the induced EMF in the circuit is zero because the magnetic flux through its area does not change.
This can also be explained as follows: when the circuit moves, forces act on the electrons in conductors $AB$ and $CD$, directed from $B$ to $A$ and from $C$ to $D$, respectively. The total work done by these forces in one clockwise or counterclockwise trip around the circuit is zero.

inventory.description: One horizontal line segment labeled B at left and C at right. The upward normal vector n starts at the intersection inside BC.
The magnetic-field vector B starts on the lower-left extension, passes through the same intersection, and has an oblique upward-right arrowhead.

The alpha arc lies between BC's positive right ray and the oblique B ray. A second arc labeled 90 degrees minus alpha lies between the oblique B ray and upward normal n. Both angle sectors share one vertex; together they span the right angle from positive BC to n.

modernAdditions: Regularize line/arc geometry with a finite common vertex and exact complementary sectors.
The illustrative oblique angle is not a numerical given and will not be labeled with its construction value.
Use standard vector labels n/B and English/math-only glyphs.
